Question_text: A student measures the refractive index of oil. Oil is poured into a semi-circular transparent plastic container as shown in Fig. 1.1. The container is placed on top of a 360° protractor as shown in Fig. 1.2.
image: Fig. 1.1 shows a semi-circular transparent plastic container with oil inside, featuring a flat side. Fig. 1.2 shows a top-down view of the semi-circular container placed on a 360° protractor. A normal line is shown, and a ray of light is incident at the midpoint of the flat side (labeled AB) with an angle of incidence i = 30°. The refracted ray in the oil is also shown, indicating the path of light from air into oil.

Parts.part_text: The line AB shows the position of the flat side of the plastic container. A ray of light is incident at the midpoint of AB with an angle of incidence i = 30° as shown in Fig. 1.2.
State one property of the oil that is needed to ensure that the experiment works.
On Fig. 1.2, measure the angle of refraction r of the light in the oil.
The student repeats the procedure described in (a) and measures the angle of refraction r for angles of incidence i = 15°, 45°, 60°, and 75°. The results are shown in Table 1.1.

Complete Table 1.1 with your value of r from (a)(ii). On the grid provided in Fig. 1.3, plot a graph of r on the y-axis against i on the x-axis. Start your axes from (0,0). Draw a smooth curve of best fit.
Parts.image: Fig. 1.3 shows an empty grid with an x-axis labeled 'i/°' and a y-axis labeled 'r/°', both starting from (0,0), intended for plotting a graph of angle of refraction (r) against angle of incidence (i).

Parts.part_text: Describe the relationship between i and r shown by the graph.
Use your graph to find the value of r when i = 50°. Show on the graph how you determine your answer.

Theory suggests that the refractive index n of the oil is given by: n = sin i / sin r. Using i and your value of r from (b)(iii), calculate a value for n. Give your answer to an appropriate number of significant figures.
On Fig. 1.4, sketch the graph when sin r is plotted against sin i. No calculations are required.
Parts.image: Fig. 1.4 shows an empty graph with the y-axis labeled 'sin r' and the x-axis labeled 'sin i', both starting from (0,0), intended for sketching the relationship between sin r and sin i.

Parts.part_text: Suggest one reason why the practical method used in this investigation might not give an accurate value for n.

Question_text: A student investigates the cooling of water. The apparatus used is shown in Fig. 2.1.
image: Fig. 2.1 shows a laboratory setup for an experiment on cooling water. It includes a thermometer immersed in water inside a 500 cm³ beaker, which is itself placed within a larger 250 cm³ beaker. A stop-clock displaying '00:00' is also visible, next to the beakers. The beakers have volume markings.

Parts.part_text: The student: pours 200 cm³ of hot water into the 500 cm³ beaker; places the thermometer in the water; stirs the water; measures the initial temperature of the water; uses the clock to find the time taken for the water to cool by 5.0°C and by 10.0°C; repeats the experiment three times.
Explain why the water is stirred before taking a temperature reading.
The student uses 200 cm³ of hot water in the same beaker in each test. State one other experimental variable that the student keeps constant to make a fair comparison of the three sets of results.
Table 2.1 shows the results obtained by the student.
Complete Table 2.1 by calculating the average time taken for the water to cool by 5.0°C. Give your answer to an appropriate number of significant figures.
Suggest one reason why the time taken for the water to cool by 10.0°C is not double the time taken for the water to cool by 5.0°C.

The student repeats the experiment using the 250 cm³ beaker. All other experimental variables remain the same. Table 2.2 shows the average times taken for the 250 cm³ beaker to cool by 5.0°C and by 10.0°C.
Describe the difference in the cooling of the water in the two beakers. Refer to the results recorded in Table 2.1 and Table 2.2 in your answer.
Suggest a reason for the difference.

Question_text: A student measures the density of a sample of modelling clay. The clay is moulded into a cube as shown in Fig. 3.1.
image: Fig. 3.1 shows a 3D isometric drawing of a perfect cube. One of its sides is labeled 'd'.

Parts.part_text: Suggest one difficulty the student finds when moulding the clay into a cube.
On Fig. 3.1, measure the length d of one side of the cube.
Calculate the volume V of the modelling clay using the equation: V = d³.
The student uses a balance to find the mass m of the modelling clay as shown in Fig. 3.2. Calculate the density ρ of the modelling clay using the equation: ρ = m / V. Give the unit of your answer.
Parts.image: Fig. 3.2 shows a digital balance displaying a measurement of '36.3 g'.

Question_text: A student investigates the current in a resistor of fixed resistance. The following apparatus is available: ammeter electrical connecting leads a resistor of fixed resistance lamp switch variable resistor 6 V battery LED voltmeter.

Parts.part_text: State which piece of apparatus is used to measure current.
The student measures the current I for a range of potential differences. Draw a circuit diagram to show the circuit the student uses. You may use some or all of the apparatus available.
Describe how the student obtains different values of the potential difference across the fixed resistor.
